title: A user can answer Yes to having a region of origin code, leave the code blank and move on to the next page with no message; DR1 stops them on the page and asks for it.

finding.frontend: Choosing Yes reveals the region of origin code box, and the page does not require it. The only check the page makes on the field is that it is at most five characters long; an empty value passes, the page saves and the user goes on to the next question with a Yes on record and no code against it, with no message anywhere on the way (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:63-82). The rule is not absent from the service — it is applied late. The obligation model makes the code mandatory whenever the requirement radio is Yes (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/origin.js), so the Origin hub row stays incomplete and the Check your answers page cannot be opened at all until the code is filled in. What the user actually meets is a Yes with no code, no explanation at the point of the mistake, and a blocked hub row later.
finding.prototype: DR1 treats the code as required the moment Yes is chosen, and says so where the mistake is made. Save and continue with the box empty returns the page with 'There is a problem' at the top and 'Enter the region of origin code' both in the summary and against the field, and the summary link moves focus into the box (app/routes.js:253-259). Answering No skips the question and nothing is asked. DR1 also carries the same rule at the two later points the frontend uses: the hub reads the origin task as complete only when the code is present under Yes (app/routes.js:231-245), and Continue on the review page is refused while it is missing (app/routes.js:10068-10075).
finding.difference: Add the page-level check the frontend is missing, so the message arrives when the user makes the mistake rather than as a stuck hub row later: make the region of origin code mandatory at submit whenever the requirement radio is Yes, with 'Enter the region of origin code' in the summary and against the field. This is a validator change on one page, not a model change — the obligation is already mandatory under Yes, so nothing downstream moves and nothing needs a new pattern. Leave the No branch alone.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting DR1's origin page with Yes selected and the code box empty and reaching the next screen.
finding.correction: Overstated; slot rewritten, claim stands in a narrower form. CLAIMED: 'nothing requires it'. TRUE: nothing on the PAGE requires it, but the obligation model marks regionOfOriginCode mandatory when regionOfOriginCodeRequirement is 'yes' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/origin.js, an equalsGate to status 'mandatory'), which feeds rowStatus in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js and readyForCheckYourAnswers in src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15 — and the whole review section sits behind that gate (flow.js:81-85). So the user cannot submit without the code; they simply are not told at the point of the mistake. DR1 enforces at all three points, the frontend only at the last two. HOW CHECKED: read the origin page validator, the origin obligation section, the status roll-up and the review gate on the frontend; read validateOriginOfImport, hasOriginDetails and the review POST on DR1.

relatedTo.why: both change the same revealed field
